newsitem.title: INDIA: Afghan refugees in India call for Taleban's ouster.
newsitem.headline: Afghan refugees in India call for Taleban's ouster.

text.p: Hundreds of Afghan refugees in India protested on Tuesday against the fall of Kabul, and said they were praying for the ouster of the Islamic Taleban militia now in control of most of war-ravaged Afghanistan.
"We are praying that the Taleban forces would be ousted soon. Then we can return to our country," said Habib Mustafa, 30, an Afghan refugee in New Delhi.

Police said more than 400 Afghan refugees, including some 70 women and two dozen children, took part in the demonstration in the Indian capital's diplomatic enclave. Police eventually used water cannon to disperse the protesters.
The refugees vented their anger against the Taleban who took control of Kabul on Friday, and blamed India's neighbour Pakistan for sponsoring terrorism in their homeland.
They burnt the Pakistani flag and shouted slogans against Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
"Pakistan, quit Afghanistan," said one banner carried by a 10-year-old Afghani boy.
Nearly 25,000 Afghans fled to India after General Najibullah was ousted from power in 1992. The Taleban executed Najibullah after overrunning Kabul last week.

"Afghanistan is our country and we will not allow others to rule over us. We will return as soon as they are thrown out of power," said Zahir Turkamani, 50, a former Afghan general who took asylum in India a year ago.
Some refugees said it would be difficult to remove the Taleban militia, who on Tuesday continued their powerful sweep across three-quarters of Afghanistan.
"As long as they have the support of agents like Pakistan, it is very difficult to overthrow them," said Shikib, 25.
The refugees lashed out at the radical rule of the Taleban, criticising the enforcement of strict Islamic rules.
"They are torturing our women. This is anti-Islamic. We do not want to go back as long as they are in power," said Saida Gharibzada, a women refugee who was in tears.

The Taleban has promised to govern Afghanistan according to Islamic Sharia law. It has banned women from working and ordered all men employed in government offices and the military to grow long beards.
Mahboobullah, 26, arrived in India on a temporary business visa just before the Taleban captured Kabul. His visa will not allow him to stay very long in India, but he was scared to go home.
"If I go back now they might execute me without any reason. I don't know what to do," he said.
